M1: Immediate Mortality (IFL_loss)

```{r}
    treecover_sc = as.numeric(scale(treecover2000)),
    def_pre_sc   = as.numeric(scale(def_prefire_3yr_mean)),
    def_post_sc   = as.numeric(scale(def_postfire_5yr_mean)),
    slope_sc     = as.numeric(scale(slope)),
    dNBR_sc      = as.numeric(scale(dNBR_yr1))
```

```{r}
library(lmerTest)
library(lme4)

table(plot_metrics_analysis$sev_MT07)

plot_metrics_analysis <- plot_metrics_analysis %>%
  mutate(
    sev_MT07 = factor(sev_MT07, 
                       levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High")), # Low burn severity should be first
    
    EVT_GP_plot = relevel(factor(EVT_GP_plot), 
                          ref = "CA Dry Mixed Conifer")
  )

m1_sc <- lmer(
  IFL_loss ~ sev_MT07 + elevation_sc + # IFL= immediate mortality,(sev_MT07) == Miller and Thode (2007) burn severity,
            sev_MT07:elevation_sc +
            treecover_sc + EVT_GP_plot +
            def_pre_sc + slope_sc +
            (sev_MT07 | Fire_ID),
  data    = plot_metrics_analysis,
  REML    = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

cat("M1 scaled R2:\n"); print(MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(m1_sc))
m1_sc
drop1(m1_sc, test = "Chisq")

car::vif(m1_sc)
```

Run a GLMM:

Helper Functions:
```{r}
# R² calculation for glmmTMB (not built-in)
r2_marginal_glmmtmb <- function(model) {
  pred_fixed <- predict(model, re.form = NA, type = "response")
  obs <- model$data[[as.character(formula(model))[2]]]
  ss_res <- sum((obs - pred_fixed)^2, na.rm = TRUE)
  ss_tot <- sum((obs - mean(obs, na.rm = TRUE))^2, na.rm = TRUE)
  1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)
}

r2_conditional_glmmtmb <- function(model) {
  pred_all <- predict(model, type = "response")
  obs <- model$data[[as.character(formula(model))[2]]]
  ss_res <- sum((obs - pred_all)^2, na.rm = TRUE)
  ss_tot <- sum((obs - mean(obs, na.rm = TRUE))^2, na.rm = TRUE)
  1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)
}
```

Gamma with log-link vs Tweedie Model
```{r}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# GAMMA GLMM for PAL (delayed mortality), log link
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#citation("DHARMa")

library(glmmTMB)
library(lme4)
library(DHARMa)  # For residual diagnostics

# Ensure PAL_loss is in m2_data (positive values for Gamma)
m2_data <- plot_metrics_analysis %>%
  filter(PAL_loss > 0, !is.na(sev_MT07))

cat("M2 n:", nrow(m2_data))

cat("PAL_loss range:", range(m2_data$PAL_loss, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Any PAL_loss == 0?", sum(m2_data$PAL_loss == 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n") #n=0


# Make sure covariate values are all there:
cc <- complete.cases(m2_data[, c("PAL_loss", "sev_MT07", "dNBR_sc", "IFL_loss",
                                 "elevation_sc", "treecover_sc", "EVT_GP_plot",
                                 "def_pre_sc", "def_post_sc", "slope_sc")])

m2_cc <- m2_data[cc, ] 

# ── Model 1: Gamma GLMM ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
m2_gamma <- glmmTMB(
  PAL_loss ~ dNBR_sc + IFL_loss + elevation_sc + dNBR_sc:elevation_sc +
    treecover_sc + EVT_GP_plot + def_pre_sc + def_post_sc + slope_sc +
    (dNBR_sc | Fire_ID),
  data = m2_cc,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  control = glmmTMBControl(optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000))
)

cat("=== GAMMA GLMM SUMMARY ===\n")
print(summary(m2_gamma))

# ── Model 2: Tweedie GLMM ───────────────────────────────────
# Final Model Eq. 2
m2_tweedie <- glmmTMB(
  PAL_loss ~ dNBR_sc +
    elevation_sc +
    dNBR_sc:elevation_sc +
    IFL_loss +
    treecover_sc +
    EVT_GP_plot +
    def_pre_sc +
    def_post_sc +
    slope_sc +
    (dNBR_sc | Fire_ID),
  data = m2_cc,
  family = tweedie(link = "log")
)

m2_tweedie

cat("\n=== TWEEDIE GLMM SUMMARY ===\n")
print(summary(m2_tweedie))

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# MODEL COMPARISON
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
library(performance)
r2(m2_gamma)
r2(m2_tweedie)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXTRACT AND COMPARE COEFFICIENTS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Get fixed effects with exponentiated (odds ratio / rate ratio) form
coef_gamma <- broom.mixed::tidy(m2_gamma, effects = "fixed", exponentiate = FALSE)
coef_tweedie <- broom.mixed::tidy(m2_tweedie, effects = "fixed", exponentiate = FALSE)

# Compare key predictors
comparison_coef <- full_join(
  coef_gamma %>% select(term, estimate, std.error, p.value) %>%
    rename(Gamma_est = estimate, Gamma_se = std.error, Gamma_p = p.value),
  coef_tweedie %>% select(term, estimate, std.error, p.value) %>%
    rename(Tweedie_est = estimate, Tweedie_se = std.error, Tweedie_p = p.value),
  by = "term"
) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    Delta_est = Gamma_est - Tweedie_est,
    Gamma_exp = round(exp(Gamma_est) - 1, 4),  # % change in PAL per SD increase
    Tweedie_exp = round(exp(Tweedie_est) - 1, 4)
  ) %>%
  select(term, Gamma_est, Tweedie_est, Delta_est, Gamma_exp, Tweedie_exp, 
         Gamma_p, Tweedie_p)

cat("\n=== COEFFICIENT COMPARISON (Gamma vs Tweedie) ===\n")
print(comparison_coef)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS: Reported in S2
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Simulate residuals for DHARMa
sim_gamma <- simulateResiduals(m2_gamma, n = 250)
sim_tweedie <- simulateResiduals(m2_tweedie, n = 250)

cat("\n=== RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS ===\n")
cat("Gamma GLMM:\n")
print(testResiduals(sim_gamma))

cat("\nTweedie GLMM:\n")
print(testResiduals(sim_tweedie))

# Visualize residuals
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(sim_gamma, main = "Gamma Residuals")
plot(sim_tweedie, main = "Tweedie Residuals")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FIXED: PREDICTION COMPARISON (handling size mismatch)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Get predictions for complete cases only
pred_comparison <- tibble(
  Observed = m2_cc$PAL_loss,
  Gamma_fitted = predict(m2_gamma, re.form = NA, type = "response"),
  Tweedie_fitted = predict(m2_tweedie, re.form = NA, type = "response")
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Observed) & !is.na(Gamma_fitted) & !is.na(Tweedie_fitted)) %>%
  summarise(
    n_obs = n(),
    Gamma_RMSE = sqrt(mean((Observed - Gamma_fitted)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Tweedie_RMSE = sqrt(mean((Observed - Tweedie_fitted)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Gamma_MAE = mean(abs(Observed - Gamma_fitted), na.rm = TRUE),
    Tweedie_MAE = mean(abs(Observed - Tweedie_fitted), na.rm = TRUE),
    Gamma_Bias = mean(Gamma_fitted - Observed, na.rm = TRUE),
    Tweedie_Bias = mean(Tweedie_fitted - Observed, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat("\n=== PREDICTION ACCURACY ===\n")
print(pred_comparison)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# COEFFICIENT COMPARISON TABLE
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

coef_gamma <- broom.mixed::tidy(m2_gamma, effects = "fixed") %>%
  dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)")
coef_tweedie <- broom.mixed::tidy(m2_tweedie, effects = "fixed") %>%
  dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)")

comparison_coef <- full_join(
  coef_gamma %>% dplyr::select(term, estimate, std.error, p.value) %>%
    rename(Gamma_est = estimate, Gamma_se = std.error, Gamma_p = p.value),
  coef_tweedie %>% dplyr::select(term, estimate, std.error, p.value) %>%
    rename(Tweedie_est = estimate, Tweedie_se = std.error, Tweedie_p = p.value),
  by = "term"
) %>%
  mutate(
    Gamma_exp = paste0(round(100 * (exp(Gamma_est) - 1), 1), "%"),
    Tweedie_exp = paste0(round(100 * (exp(Tweedie_est) - 1), 1), "%"),
    Gamma_sig = ifelse(Gamma_p < 0.001, "***", 
                      ifelse(Gamma_p < 0.01, "**", 
                            ifelse(Gamma_p < 0.05, "*", ""))),
    Tweedie_sig = ifelse(Tweedie_p < 0.001, "***", 
                        ifelse(Tweedie_p < 0.01, "**", 
                              ifelse(Tweedie_p < 0.05, "*", "")))
  ) %>%
  select(term, Gamma_est, Gamma_exp, Gamma_sig, 
         Tweedie_est, Tweedie_exp, Tweedie_sig)

cat("\n=== FIXED EFFECTS COMPARISON ===\n")
print(comparison_coef)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SUMMARY TABLE
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

cat("\n╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
cat("║              MODEL COMPARISON: GAMMA vs TWEEDIE                ║\n")
cat("╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")

summary_table <- tribble(
  ~Metric,                    ~Gamma,           ~Tweedie,
  "AIC",                      "77267.8",        "75231.4",
  "ΔAIC vs best",             "+2,036",          "0 (best)",
  "BIC",                      "77428.0",        "75398.9",
  "logLik",                   "-38611.9",       "-37592.7",
  "Dispersion/Sigma",         "0.328",          "1.26",
  "Convergence",              "✓ Yes",          "✓ Yes",
  "RMSE (pred)",              format(pred_comparison$Gamma_RMSE[1], digits=3),
                              format(pred_comparison$Tweedie_RMSE[1], digits=3),
  "MAE (pred)",               format(pred_comparison$Gamma_MAE[1], digits=3),
                              format(pred_comparison$Tweedie_MAE[1], digits=3),
  "Prediction Bias",          format(pred_comparison$Gamma_Bias[1], digits=4),
                              format(pred_comparison$Tweedie_Bias[1], digits=4),
  "Residual Outliers (p)",    "—",              "0.3283 (✓ Good)"
)

print(summary_table)
```

Report Tweedie emmeans--> TableS4
this is the back-transformed Tweedie_estimate and can be reported as is without calculating exp*# etc.
```{r}
library(emmeans)

# 1. Simple def_post contrast
emm_defpost <- emmeans(
  m2_tweedie,
  ~ def_post_sc,
  at = list(
    def_post_sc = c(0, 1),
    dNBR_sc = 0,
    elevation_sc = 0
  ),
  type = "response",
  re.form = NA  # Population-level predictions
)
contrast(
  emm_defpost,
  method = "revpairwise",
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
)

# 2. Helper function (add re.form = NA)
ratio_effect <- function(model, var, values = c(0, 1),
                         by = NULL, at_extra = list()) {
  at_list <- at_extra
  at_list[[var]] <- values
  specs <- if (is.null(by)) {
    as.formula(paste("~", var))
  } else {
    as.formula(paste("~", var, "|", paste(by, collapse = " * ")))
  }
  emm <- emmeans(
    model,
    specs = specs,
    at = at_list,
    type = "response",
    re.form = NA  # Population-level predictions
  )
  contrast(
    emm,
    method = "revpairwise",
    ratio = TRUE,
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
  )
}

# 3. Standardized continuous covariates
treecover_result <- ratio_effect(
  m2_tweedie,
  "treecover_sc",
  at_extra = list(dNBR_sc = 0, elevation_sc = 0)
)
def_pre_result <- ratio_effect(
  m2_tweedie,
  "def_pre_sc",
  at_extra = list(dNBR_sc = 0, elevation_sc = 0)
)
def_post_result <- ratio_effect(
  m2_tweedie,
  "def_post_sc",
  at_extra = list(dNBR_sc = 0, elevation_sc = 0)
)
slope_result <- ratio_effect(
  m2_tweedie,
  "slope_sc",
  at_extra = list(dNBR_sc = 0, elevation_sc = 0)
)

treecover_result # print the values to report
def_pre_result
def_post_result
slope_result

# 4. IFL (continuous)
ifl_result <- ratio_effect(
  m2_tweedie,
  "IFL_loss",
  at_extra = list(dNBR_sc = 0, elevation_sc = 0)
)
ifl_result

# 5. dNBR by elevation (interacting term)
dnbr_by_elevation <- ratio_effect(
  m2_tweedie,
  "dNBR_sc",
  values = c(0, 1),
  by = "elevation_sc",
  at_extra = list(
    elevation_sc = c(-1, 0, 1)
  )
)
dnbr_by_elevation

# 6. Elevation by dNBR (interacting term)
elevation_by_dnbr <- ratio_effect(
  m2_tweedie,
  "elevation_sc",
  values = c(0, 1),
  by = "dNBR_sc",
  at_extra = list(
    dNBR_sc = c(0, 1, 2) # mean, moderate, high urn severity
  )
)
elevation_by_dnbr

# 7. Vegetation type (categorical, no interactions with continuous predictors)
vegetation_result <- emmeans(
  m2_tweedie,
  ~ EVT_GP_plot,
  at = list(
    dNBR_sc = 0,
    elevation_sc = 0
  ),
  type = "response",
  re.form = NA  # Population-level predictions
) %>%
  contrast(
    method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
    ref = 1,
    ratio = TRUE,
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
  )
vegetation_result

library(performance)

# Marginal R² (fixed effects only)

r2(m2_tweedie)
```

These are the raw values that have yet to be transformed for you
```{r}
# ============================================================
# 2) Back-transformed effects with asymmetric CIs (emmeans)
#    Model: (Tweedie, log link, PAL_loss)
# ============================================================

# Reference profile: dNBR_sc = 0 (mean dNBR), reference EVT class,
# IFL at its mean (typical immediate loss), all other scaled

# continuous predictors at 0 (their means)
base_at <- list(dNBR_sc = 0,
                IFL = mean(m2_cc$IFL),        # ~ -17.8 pp
                elevation_sc = 0, treecover_sc = 0,
                def_pre_sc = 0, def_post_sc = 0, slope_sc = 0)

# --- dNBR dose-response: predicted PAL (%) at mean, +1 SD, +2 SD ---
at_dnbr <- base_at
at_dnbr$dNBR_sc <- c(0, 1, 2)
emm_dnbr <- emmeans(m2_tweedie, "dNBR_sc", at = at_dnbr, type = "response")
emm_dnbr

# per +1 SD multiplicative effect of dNBR (ratio, asymmetric CI)
at_dnbr1 <- base_at
at_dnbr1$dNBR_sc <- c(0, 1)
contrast(emmeans(m2_tweedie, "dNBR_sc", at = at_dnbr1), "pairwise", type = "response")

# --- Continuous predictors: predicted PAL at 0 vs +1 SD ---
cont_vars <- c("IFL", "elevation_sc", "treecover_sc",
               "def_pre_sc", "def_post_sc", "slope_sc")

for (v in cont_vars) {
  at_v <- base_at
  at_v[[v]] <- c(0, 1)
  cat("\n=====", v, "=====\n")
  # back-transformed predictions (asymmetric CIs)
  print(emmeans(m2_tweedie, v, at = at_v, type = "response"))
  # percentage-point difference at the reference profile
  emm_link <- emmeans(m2_tweedie, v, at = at_v)
  print(contrast(regrid(emm_link), "pairwise"))
}

# --- Interaction dNBR x elevation: dNBR effect at elevation 0 and +1 SD ---
at_int <- list(dNBR_sc = c(0, 1),
               IFL = mean(m2_cc$IFL),
               treecover_sc = 0, def_pre_sc = 0, def_post_sc = 0, slope_sc = 0,
               elevation_sc = c(0, 1))

emm_int <- emmeans(m2_tweedie, ~ dNBR_sc | elevation_sc, at = at_int, type = "response")
emm_int
# dNBR ratio (+1 SD) within each elevation level:
contrast(emmeans(m2_tweedie, ~ dNBR_sc | elevation_sc, at = at_int),
         "pairwise", type = "response")

#exp(0.3)
```
eg. 
==== IFL =====
 IFL response    SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
   0     21.6 0.475 Inf      20.6      22.5 --> 0 is at the mean value
   1     21.9 0.485 Inf      21.0      22.9 --> 1 SD increase
   

With a log link, type = "response" back-transforms predictions to the original percentage-point scale and gives asymmetric CIs (the endpoints are back-transformed from the link scale), which is what you want instead of the symmetric delta-method CIs. The pairwise contrasts on a log link come out as ratios (e.g., High severity predicts PAL 2.1x higher than Low); the regrid() contrasts give the percentage-point differences at the reference profile. Because the back-transform is multiplicative, the percentage-point effect of any predictor depends on the baseline level, so report the reference profile explicitly and treat the numbers as conditional on it.

#Example 1. 
"Predicted delayed canopy loss was 16.1% (95% CI: 15.5-16.8%) at mean burn severity (dNBR), averaged across vegetation types, with all other covariates at their means. Delayed loss increased steeply with burn severity: each 1 SD increase in dNBR was associated with a 1.48-fold (95% CI: 1.45-1.51) increase in delayed loss, with predicted loss reaching 23.9% (95% CI: 22.9-25.0%) at +1 SD and 35.4% (95% CI: 33.5-37.4%) at +2 SD dNBR."

The 1.48 is the inverse of the 0.675 ratio emmeans printed (1/0.675 = 1.48), which is the per-SD multiplicative effect from the log link. The three percentages are the back-transformed predictions from your dose-response table.

The delta method is a first-order linear approximation — it assumes the transformation is locally close to linear near the estimated coefficients. For a simple squaring transform with parameter estimates well away from zero (which yours appear to be, since your baseline is ~3.46 on the sqrt scale), this approximation is generally solid. If you want to double check robustness, especially for interaction terms with small/uncertain estimates, a parametric bootstrap (bootMer() in lme4, refitting and back-transforming each bootstrap replicate) would be a heavier-weight but assumption-free alternative — worth mentioning as a footnote or sensitivity check rather than redoing everything by default.

Mixed severity refuge effect?

Dense stands are large enough to contain:

High-severity patches (burn hot, lose canopy fast)
Low-severity refugia (burn cool, trees die slowly from sub-lethal injury)

The low-severity component drags out the overall plot trajectory:

Dense plot = mosaic of fast-dying (high sev) + slow-dying (low sev) = longer tail
Sparse plot = more uniform (if it burns at all, burns consistently) = faster min reach

The complete-case set is now clean and interpretable: 11,303 plots (one row each ✓), zero out-of-range values, and structural endpoints: 566 plots at exactly 0 (no measurable delayed loss) and 1,318 at exactly 1 (no measurable immediate loss, i.e., canopy at year 1 at or above baseline, then declining). That's 16.7% of the modeling sample sitting on the boundaries, and both spikes are meaningful ecological groups worth reporting descriptively, not noise to be smoothed away.

```{r}
library(emmeans)

# 1. Simple def_post contrast
emm_defpost <- emmeans(
  m3_ordered_beta,
  ~ def_post_sc,
  at = list(
    def_post_sc = c(0, 1),
    dNBR_sc = 0,
    elevation_sc = 0
  ),
  type = "response",
  re.form = NA  # Population-level predictions
)
contrast(
  emm_defpost,
  method = "revpairwise",
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
)

# 2. Helper function (add re.form = NA)
ratio_effect <- function(model, var, values = c(0, 1),
                         by = NULL, at_extra = list()) {
  at_list <- at_extra
  at_list[[var]] <- values
  specs <- if (is.null(by)) {
    as.formula(paste("~", var))
  } else {
    as.formula(paste("~", var, "|", paste(by, collapse = " * ")))
  }
  emm <- emmeans(
    model,
    specs = specs,
    at = at_list,
    type = "response",
    re.form = NA  # Population-level predictions
  )
  contrast(
    emm,
    method = "revpairwise",
    ratio = TRUE,
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
  )
}

# 3. Standardized continuous covariates

  "treecover_sc",

)

 m3_ordered_beta,

)

)
```

#You need to report the Time ratio (not odds ratio); calculate the TR and the Beta, SE for reporting: M4

Get the TR - percentage of change over time:

TR > 1 → longer survival time (deceleration)
TR < 1 → shorter survival time (acceleration)

To express the effect as a percent change in survival time:
If TR < 1
(1 - TR) * 100

If TR > 1:
(TR - 1) * 100

#Get Beta coefficients, SE, CI, p-values from survreg() and Percent Change M3 (Supplemental Table 4) 
```{r}
m4_summary <- summary(m_aft_int)
m4_table   <- as.data.frame(m4_summary$table)

# Covariate names are stored as rownames — pull them explicitly
covariate <- rownames(m4_table)

beta     <- m4_table$Value
se       <- m4_table$`Std. Error`
z_stat   <- m4_table$z
p_val    <- m4_table$p

TR       <- exp(beta)
TR_lower <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
TR_upper <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)

pct_change <- ifelse(TR < 1, (1 - TR) * 100, (TR - 1) * 100)
direction  <- ifelse(TR < 1, "Shorter survival", "Longer survival")

results <- data.frame(
  Covariate      = covariate,          # ← now first column
  Beta           = round(beta, 3),
  SE             = round(se, 3),
  TR             = round(TR, 3),
  CI_lower       = round(TR_lower, 3),
  CI_upper       = round(TR_upper, 3),
  Percent_Change = round(pct_change, 1),
  Direction      = direction,
  p_value        = signif(p_val, 3)
)

print(results)

rownames(m4_summary$table)
results <- results %>% 
  filter(Covariate != "Log(scale)")
```

# Supplemental M4: testing Weibull distribution and Cox Proportional Hazards (PH) model:
For a Weibull PH model:
h(t)=λρt
ρ−1

Since:
rho > 1, the hazard increases (accelerates) through time.

In a PH Weibull frailty model:
negative coefficient → lower hazard
lower hazard → slower time to minimum canopy

You should now check whether severity effects change through time.
Because ecologically:
high severity may cause rapid early decline,
low severity may produce delayed mortality --> which violates proportional hazards.
```{r}
library(survival)
library(coxme)

m_weibull <- survreg(
  Surv(min_year, event_observed) ~
    dNBR_sc + sev_MT07 + treecover_sc + EVT_GP_plot + def_pre_sc + def_post_sc + elevation_sc + slope_sc,
  data = plot_metrics_analysis,
  dist = "weibull"
)

m_weibull 

# Fixed Cox Proportional Hazards model
m_cox <- coxph(
  Surv(min_year, event_observed) ~
    dNBR_sc +
    sev_MT07 +
    treecover_sc +
    EVT_GP_plot+
    def_pre_sc +
    def_post_sc +
    elevation_sc +
    slope_sc +
    cluster(Fire_ID),
  data = plot_metrics_analysis
)
m_cox

# Mixed Effects or Frailty Cox Model
m_coxme <- coxme(
  Surv(min_year, event_observed) ~
    dNBR_sc +
    sev_MT07 +
    treecover_sc +
    EVT_GP_plot +
    def_pre_sc +
    def_post_sc +
    elevation_sc +
    slope_sc +
    (1 | Fire_ID), # this adds a random intercept (frailty) per fire into the hazard function
  data = plot_metrics_analysis
)
m_coxme

# Lognormal AFT Model
m_aft <- survreg(
  Surv(min_year, event_observed) ~
    dNBR_sc +
    sev_MT07 +
    treecover_sc +
    EVT_GP_plot + 
    def_pre_sc +
    def_post_sc +
    elevation_sc +
    slope_sc,
  data = plot_metrics_analysis,
  dist = "lognormal"
)

summary(m_aft)

# convert the AFT coefficients to time ratios:
exp(coef(m_aft))
#1 → slower decline / delayed canopy minimum
#<1 → faster decline

# Test the ME Cox Proportional Hazards:
ph_test <- cox.zph(m_cox)

print(ph_test)
plot(ph_test)

AIC(m_weibull, m_cox, m_coxme, m_aft) 
```

if p-value is significant--> That means the Cox PH assumption does not hold for your data overall.

And several individual predictors violate PH too:
sev_class
EVT_GP_collapsed
def_post_sc
slope_sc

This is because the above variables are Time varying and So hazard ratios change through time.

From the PH plots:
For each variable:

flat horizontal line → PH okay
systematic trend/slope → PH violated

#M5 (delayed dominant "proportion of delayed mortality" low loss and high mortality loss)

First run the         
Odds Ratio Function:
```{r}
get_or_table <- function(model) {
  coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients

  z <- coefs[, "z value"]
  p <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z)))

  data.frame(
    term = rownames(coefs),
    estimate = coefs[, "Estimate"],
    se = coefs[, "Std. Error"],
    OR = exp(coefs[, "Estimate"]),
    conf.low = exp(coefs[, "Estimate"] - 1.96 * coefs[, "Std. Error"]),
    conf.high = exp(coefs[, "Estimate"] + 1.96 * coefs[, "Std. Error"]),
    p_value = p
  )
}
```
INTERPRETATION
OR value	meaning
OR > 1	increases probability of delayed dominance
OR < 1	decreases probability (pushes toward immediate dominance)
OR = 1	no effect
This is your within-low-severity mechanism model

Create dt3 data frame 
```{r}

  default = NA_character_
)]

# 2. Delayed dominance outcome (GLOBAL definition)

names(dt3)
```

Data Integrity Checks:
```{r}
install.packages("rlang")
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# Read in new plots
new_plots <- read.csv("All_202_Wildfire_Plots_Stratified_90m.csv")

# ── 1. ROW COUNTS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("Total rows:", nrow(new_plots), "\n")
cat("Expected: ~30,000-40,000, 202 fires")

# ── 2. FIRE COUNTS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("Unique fires:", n_distinct(new_plots$Fire_ID), "\n")
cat("Expected: 202\n\n")

# ── 3. CATEGORY BALANCE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
table(new_plots$Category)
# Expected: roughly equal FP and BP counts

# ── 4. POINTS PER FIRE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
new_plots %>%
  group_by(Fire_ID, Fire_Name, Category) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  summarise(
    min_plots = min(n),
    median_plots = median(n),
    mean_plots = mean(n),
    max_plots = max(n)
  )
# Expected: min=30, max=200, balanced between FP and BP

# ── 5. COORDINATE INTEGRITY ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Parse .geo and extract centroids using your clean pipeline
new_plots <- new_plots %>%
  mutate(.geo_clean = gsub('""', '"', .geo)) %>%
  mutate(
    geo_parsed = lapply(.geo_clean, function(x) {
      if (is.na(x) | x == "") return(NULL)
      tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON(x), error = function(e) NULL)
    }),
    long = sapply(geo_parsed, function(g) {
      if (is.null(g)) return(NA)
      coords <- g$coordinates
      # Handle both Point [lon,lat] and Polygon [[[lon,lat],...]] geometries
      if (g$type == "Point") {
        round(coords[1], 6)
      } else {
        round(mean(coords[1,,1]), 6)
      }
    }),
    lat = sapply(geo_parsed, function(g) {
      if (is.null(g)) return(NA)
      coords <- g$coordinates
      if (g$type == "Point") {
        round(coords[2], 6)
      } else {
        round(mean(coords[1,,2]), 6)
      }
    })
  ) %>%
  select(-geo_parsed, -.geo_clean)

# Verify
cat("NA longitudes:", sum(is.na(new_plots$long)), "\n")
cat("Long range:", range(new_plots$long, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Lat range:", range(new_plots$lat, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# ── 6. MINIMUM DISTANCE CHECK ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Spot check one fire - verify 90m minimum distance was enforced
test_fire <- new_plots %>%
  filter(Fire_ID == first(Fire_ID)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(3310)

# Get minimum distance between any two points
dists <- st_distance(test_fire)
diag(dists) <- NA  # ignore self-distance
cat("Min distance in test fire:", min(dists, na.rm = TRUE), "m\n")
cat("Expected: >= 90m\n\n")

# ── 7. WATER CHECK ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Verify no points fall in ocean (rough check using CA bounding box)
water_suspect <- new_plots %>%
  filter(long < -124.5 | long > -114.1 | lat < 32.5 | lat > 42.0)
cat("Points outside CA bounding box:", nrow(water_suspect), "\n")
cat("Expected: 0\n\n")

# ── 8. DUPLICATE POINTS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
dupes <- new_plots %>%
  count(Fire_ID, long, lat) %>%
  filter(n > 1)
cat("Duplicate coordinates within fires:", nrow(dupes), "\n")
cat("Expected: 0\n\n")

# ── 9. FIRES WITH FEWER POINTS THAN EXPECTED ───────────────────────────────────
low_count_fires <- new_plots %>%
  group_by(Fire_ID, Fire_Name, Category) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n < 30)
cat("Fire-category combos below minimum (30):", nrow(low_count_fires), "\n")
print(low_count_fires)
```

```{r}

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Plot Classification Pipeline
# Classifies 56-m buffered plots (fire perimeter + surrounding buffer) by their
# spatial/temporal intersection history with MTBS fire perimeters (1984-2024).
#
# INPUTS (not redistributed here — see README for sources):
#   - Plot_Polygons_56m_2026.shp        : 56-m buffered sample plots (fire + buffer)
#                                          generated via Google Earth Engine
#                                          (GEE code: [https://github.com/bhays4days/delayed-mortality-california.git])
#   - Focal_Fires_And_Donuts_195.shp    : focal fire perimeters + surrounding
#                                          buffer "donuts" for the n=195 fires
#                                          sampled (also GEE-derived)
#   - mtbs_perims_DD.shp                : MTBS national fire perimeter database,
#                                          1984-2024, publicly available at
#                                          https://www.mtbs.gov/direct-download
#
# OUTPUT: plots_classified — one row per plot, with Correct_Plot_Label_final
#         giving each plot's final classification (Burned_clean, Unburned_clean,
#         Burned_Previously, Will_Burn, and edge-case categories).
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

#path <- "path/to/shapefiles/"   # <-- set to local directory

path <- "C:/Users/bhays5/Desktop/CalFire/Raw_221/"  # check your directory for .shp files.
ff <- list.files(path, pattern='\\.shp$', full.names=TRUE) # calling .shp files from the working directory
ff # Viewing a list of the working directory .shp files.
```

Fix CRS projection so they match:
```{r}
# ── Extract coordinates from plots_sf BEFORE the join ─────────────────────────
# ── Diagnose geometry type ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

           value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE))

# ── Use buffer polygons for intersection, not centroids ───────────────────────
#a plot is classified as intersecting a fire if any part of the 56m buffer overlaps the MTBS polygon boundary
# plots_sf is already polygons (33,087 × 56m buffers) — use directly
# Just reproject to planar CRS to avoid the spherical geometry warning

plots_sf_proj      <- st_transform(plots_sf,      crs = 3310)
mtbs_sf_clean_proj <- st_transform(mtbs_sf_clean, crs = 3310)

cat("plots_sf_proj geometry type:\n")
```

Spatial Intersection
```{r}
# ── Spatial join using buffer polygons ────────────────────────────────────────
mtbs_intersection <- st_join(
  plots_sf_proj,
  mtbs_sf_clean_proj %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c(
    "Event_ID", "Fire_ID",
    "Incid_Name", "Fire_Name",
    "Ig_Date", "Ig_Year",
    "BurnBndAc", "Zone"
  ))),
  join = st_intersects,   # any overlap between buffer and fire polygon
  left = TRUE
)

cat("Rows after intersection:", nrow(mtbs_intersection), "\n")

# Expect ~33,087 to ~48,000 intersections depending on multiple polygon matches
```

##Plot categorization w/ Revisions (no "Reburn plot")
The focal year is extracted from Fire_ID directly using substr(Fire_ID, 14, 17) rather than joining from new_plots_clean, which avoids a potential join duplication issue if that table has multiple rows per fire.
```{r}
# ── Add focal year from plots ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
focal_year_lookup <- plots_sf %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(
    plot_key   = paste(Fire_ID, round(long, 6), round(lat, 6), Category, sep = "_"),
    focal_year = as.integer(substr(Fire_ID, 14, 17))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(plot_key, focal_year) %>%
  distinct()

burn_history <- burn_history %>%
  left_join(focal_year_lookup, by = "plot_key")

cat("Missing focal_year:", sum(is.na(burn_history$focal_year)), "\n")

# ── Flag intersections and unnest fire years ───────────────────────────────────
plots_flagged <- burn_history %>%
  mutate(
    Intersected     = ifelse(n_fires_intersected == 0, "No", "Yes"),
    MTBS_Fire_Years = ifelse(fire_years == "", "None", fire_years)
  )

data_long <- plots_flagged %>%
  filter(Intersected == "Yes", MTBS_Fire_Years != "None") %>%
  mutate(MTBS_Year_List = strsplit(MTBS_Fire_Years, ",\\s*")) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(MTBS_Year_List) %>%
  mutate(
    MTBS_Fire_Year = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(MTBS_Year_List))),
    Year_Diff      = MTBS_Fire_Year - focal_year,
    Fire_Timing    = case_when(
      Year_Diff < 0  ~ "Before_FireYear",
      Year_Diff == 0 ~ "Same_Year_As_FireYear",
      Year_Diff > 0  ~ "After_FireYear"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(MTBS_Fire_Year))

timing_summary <- data_long %>%
  group_by(plot_key, Fire_ID, Fire_Name, Category, focal_year) %>%
  summarise(
    Min_Year_Diff     = min(Year_Diff),
    Max_Year_Diff     = max(Year_Diff),
    Fire_Timing_Flags = paste(unique(Fire_Timing), collapse = ";"),
    Earliest_Fire     = min(MTBS_Fire_Year),
    Latest_Fire       = max(MTBS_Fire_Year),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

plots_classified <- plots_flagged %>%
  left_join(
    timing_summary %>%
      dplyr::select(plot_key, Min_Year_Diff, Max_Year_Diff,
             Fire_Timing_Flags, Earliest_Fire, Latest_Fire),
    by = "plot_key"
  )

# ── Final classification — revised  ───────────────────────
# Removes "Reburned" as a standalone category
# All FP plots with additional fires are classified by TIMING of those fires
# relative to focal year — matching advisor's requested 4-category structure

plots_classified <- plots_classified %>%
  mutate(
    Correct_Plot_Label_final = case_when(

      # ── BP: UNBURNED CONTROLS ──────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Never intersects any MTBS fire
      Category == "BP" & Intersected == "No" ~ "Unburned_clean",

      # Burns only after focal year → will burn
      Category == "BP" &
        grepl("After_FireYear",   Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        !grepl("Before_FireYear|Same_Year_As_FireYear",
                Fire_Timing_Flags) ~ "Will_Burn",

      # Burns only before focal year → burned previously
      Category == "BP" &
        grepl("Before_FireYear",  Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        !grepl("After_FireYear|Same_Year_As_FireYear",
                Fire_Timing_Flags) ~ "Burned_Previously",

      # Burns in focal year — edge plot inside fire boundary
      Category == "BP" &
        grepl("Same_Year_As_FireYear",
               Fire_Timing_Flags) ~ "BP_In_Focal_Fire",

      # Burns before AND after (no focal) → burned previously
      # classifies by earliest contamination relative to observation window
      Category == "BP" &
        grepl("Before_FireYear", Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        grepl("After_FireYear",  Fire_Timing_Flags) ~ "Burned_Previously",

      # ── FP: BURNED PLOTS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Only intersects focal fire year → clean single-fire exposure
      Category == "FP" &
        grepl("Same_Year_As_FireYear", Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        !grepl("Before_FireYear|After_FireYear",
                Fire_Timing_Flags) ~ "Burned_clean",

      # Focal fire + burns after → will burn
      # Post-focal reburn is primary confound in ±10yr observation window
      Category == "FP" &
        grepl("Same_Year_As_FireYear", Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        grepl("After_FireYear",        Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        !grepl("Before_FireYear",      Fire_Timing_Flags) ~ "Will_Burn",

      # Focal fire + burned before → burned previously
      Category == "FP" &
        grepl("Same_Year_As_FireYear", Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        grepl("Before_FireYear",       Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        !grepl("After_FireYear",       Fire_Timing_Flags) ~ "Burned_Previously",

      # Focal fire + before + after → will burn
      # Post-focal reburn takes precedence as primary confound
      Category == "FP" &
        grepl("Same_Year_As_FireYear", Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        grepl("Before_FireYear",       Fire_Timing_Flags) &
        grepl("After_FireYear",        Fire_Timing_Flags) ~ "Will_Burn",

      # FP doesn't intersect focal year — geometry edge case
      Category == "FP" &
        !grepl("Same_Year_As_FireYear",
                Fire_Timing_Flags) ~ "FP_Off_Target",

      # FP no intersection at all — should not occur but catch it
      Category == "FP" & Intersected == "No" ~ "FP_No_Intersection",

      TRUE ~ "Check"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# ── Recalculate reburn timing using ONLY post-focal intersections ──────────────
# Need to look at how far AFTER the focal fire these plots reburn
# not the minimum year difference across all intersections

will_burn_fp_timing <- data_long %>%
  filter(
    plot_key %in% (plots_classified %>% 
                     filter(Category == "FP", 
                            Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Will_Burn") %>% 
                     pull(plot_key)),
    Fire_Timing == "After_FireYear"   # only post-focal intersections
  ) %>%
  group_by(plot_key) %>%
  summarise(
    yrs_to_reburn      = min(Year_Diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    reburn_year        = min(MTBS_Fire_Year, na.rm = TRUE),
    focal_year         = first(focal_year),
```

Reclassify Will_Burn FP (fire perimeter/ burned plots) plots based on reburn timing 
```{r}
# ── Reclassify Will_Burn FP plots based on reburn timing ──────────────────────
# Join disposition back to plots_classified

  left_join(
    will_burn_fp_final %>% 
      select(plot_key, yrs_to_reburn, reburn_disposition),
    by = "plot_key"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Correct_Plot_Label_final = case_when(
      
      # Will_Burn FP: reclassify by reburn timing
      Category == "FP" & 
        Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Will_Burn" &
        yrs_to_reburn > 10  ~ "Burned_clean",      # reburns after window — retain
      
      Category == "FP" & 
        Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Will_Burn" &
        yrs_to_reburn > 5 & 
        yrs_to_reburn <= 10 ~ "Burned_clean_flagged", # late window — retain with flag
      
      Category == "FP" & 
        Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Will_Burn" &
        yrs_to_reburn <= 5  ~ "Will_Burn_excluded",   # early reburn — exclude
      
      # All other classifications unchanged
      TRUE ~ Correct_Plot_Label_final
    )
  )

cat("=== FINAL CLASSIFICATION WITH REBURN TIMING ===\n")
print(
  plots_classified %>%
    count(Correct_Plot_Label_final) %>%
    mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%

)
```

The question is whether your BP (buffer perimeter/ unburned) "Will_Burn" plots are genuinely unsuitable as unburned controls or whether the buffer approach is over-flagging them. The same logic you used for FP (fire perimeter/ burned plots) applies here — if a BP  plot doesn't burn until 12 years after the focal fire, it's a valid unburned control for your ±10-year observation window. Excluding it wastes data.
```{r}
# ── Decision point: apply same reburn timing logic to BP plots ─────────────────
# If Will_Burn BP plots reburn AFTER the observation window
# they are valid unburned controls for the ±10yr window
# Same logic you applied to FP plots

plots_classified <- plots_classified %>%
  left_join(
    will_burn_bp_low %>%
      rename(yrs_to_burn_bp = yrs_to_burn),
    by = "plot_key"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Correct_Plot_Label_final = case_when(

      # Will_Burn BP that reburns after observation window — retain as control
      Category == "BP" &
        Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Will_Burn" &
        !is.na(yrs_to_burn_bp) &
        yrs_to_burn_bp > 10              ~ "Unburned_clean",

      # Will_Burn BP that reburns within window — keep excluded
      Category == "BP" &
        Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Will_Burn" &
        !is.na(yrs_to_burn_bp) &
        yrs_to_burn_bp <= 10             ~ "Will_Burn",

      # Everything else unchanged
      TRUE ~ Correct_Plot_Label_final
    )
  )
```

Originally burned plots — reburn within 10 years
```{r}
fp_10yr <- data_long %>%
  filter(Category == "FP") %>%
  group_by(plot_key) %>%
  summarise(
    focal_year = first(focal_year),
    min_postfire_year = ifelse(
      any(Year_Diff > 0),
      min(Year_Diff[Year_Diff > 0]),
      NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    reburn_within_10yr = !is.na(min_postfire_year) &
                         min_postfire_year <= 10
  )

fp_10yr %>%
  summarise(
    n_plots = n(),
    n_reburn_10yr = sum(reburn_within_10yr),
    pct_reburn_10yr = 100 * mean(reburn_within_10yr)
  )
```

Table 3 Summary table data:
```{r}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#TABLE 3 CLIMATE SUMMARY — 
# Reproduces climate rows of Table 3 using Burned_clean + Unburned_clean plots,
# one row per unique plot (static vars) or mean across all plot-years (annual vars)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

cat("\n── Table 3: Table 3 climate summary statistics ───────────────────────────\n")

# Helper: mean ± SD string
ms <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  sprintf("M=%.3f, SD=%.3f", mean(x), sd(x))
}

# Subset to clean plots only
clean <- master%>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final %in% c("Burned_clean", "Unburned_clean"))

# Static (one row per plot — use distinct)
static <- clean %>%
  distinct(plot_key, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Annual timeseries — one row per plot-year
annual <- clean  # full long format

cat("\n[ANNUAL TIMESERIES VARIABLES]\n")
cat("Annual CWD (def_ann_sum):           ", ms(annual$def_ann_sum),       "\n")
cat("CWD anomaly (def_anomaly):          ", ms(annual$def_anomaly),       "\n")
cat("SWE April max (swe_april_max):      ", ms(annual$swe_april_max),     "\n")
cat("SWE anomaly:                        ", ms(annual$swe_anomaly),       "\n")
cat("VPD ann mean (vpd_ann_mean):        ", ms(annual$vpd_ann_mean),      "\n")
cat("VPD anomaly:                        ", ms(annual$vpd_anomaly),       "\n")
cat("PDSI ann mean (pdsi_ann_mean):      ", ms(annual$pdsi_ann_mean),     "\n")
cat("PDSI anomaly:                       ", ms(annual$pdsi_anomaly),      "\n")
cat("TMMX max growing season:            ", ms(annual$tmmx_max_growing),  "\n")
cat("TMMX mean Jul-Aug:                  ", ms(annual$tmmx_mean_JulAug),  "\n")
cat("Growing season temp anomaly:        ", ms(annual$tmmx_gs_anomaly),   "\n")
cat("Jul-Aug temp anomaly:               ", ms(annual$tmmx_ja_anomaly),   "\n")

cat("\n[30-YR NORMALS — static per plot]\n")
cat("30yr CWD normal (def_normal_ann):   ", ms(static$def_normal_ann),           "\n")
cat("30yr SWE normal (swe_normal_april): ", ms(static$swe_normal_april),         "\n")
cat("30yr VPD normal:                    ", ms(static$vpd_normal_ann),           "\n")
cat("30yr PDSI normal:                   ", ms(static$pdsi_normal_ann),          "\n")
cat("30yr max growing season temp:       ", ms(static$tmmx_normal_max_growing),  "\n")
cat("30yr Jul-Aug max temp:              ", ms(static$tmmx_normal_JulAug),       "\n")

cat("\n[PRE/POST FIRE ANOMALY SUMMARIES — static per plot]\n")
cat("Pre-fire 3yr mean CWD anomaly:      ", ms(static$def_prefire_3yr_mean),   "\n")
cat("Post-fire 5yr mean CWD anomaly:     ", ms(static$def_postfire_5yr_mean),  "\n")

cat("\n✓ Table 3 climate summary complete.\n")

# ── Spot-check against Table 3 expected values ─────────────────────────────
cat("\n── Spot-check vs. Table 3 expected values ──────────────────────────────\n")

checks <- list(
  list(label = "def_ann_sum mean",    obs = mean(annual$def_ann_sum,   na.rm=TRUE), exp = 542.4, tol = 20),
  list(label = "swe_april_max mean",  obs = mean(annual$swe_april_max, na.rm=TRUE), exp = 13.7,  tol = 5),
  list(label = "vpd_ann_mean mean",   obs = mean(annual$vpd_ann_mean,  na.rm=TRUE), exp = 0.83,  tol = 0.05),
  list(label = "pdsi_ann_mean mean",  obs = mean(annual$pdsi_ann_mean, na.rm=TRUE), exp = -0.17, tol = 0.3),
  list(label = "tmmx_max_growing mean", obs = mean(annual$tmmx_max_growing, na.rm=TRUE), exp = 29.1, tol = 1),
  list(label = "def_normal_ann mean", obs = mean(static$def_normal_ann, na.rm=TRUE), exp = 535.7, tol = 30)
)

for (chk in checks) {
  pass <- abs(chk$obs - chk$exp) <= chk$tol
  status <- if (pass) "✓ PASS" else "✗ FAIL — CHECK SCALING"
  cat(sprintf("  %s: observed=%.3f, expected=%.3f  %s\n",
              chk$label, chk$obs, chk$exp, status))
}
```

# Table 3.
How the EVT codes were created:
#Code-based harmonization (no EVT names needed)
#* Recall LANDFIRE version was matched to fire year in GEE at extraction time:
LF 2001 == "1" and LF 2014 == "2"
```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

#evt_official <- read_csv("C:/Users/bhays5/Desktop/CalFire/Raw_221/us_105evt.csv") # this is the Landfire EVT 2001 data
```

```{r}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EVT GROUPING - MASTER DATA FRAME
# 
# Regroup EVT codes to match publication table groupings
# Rare types pooled into "Other Forest" (~1%)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── CREATE EVT_GP_PLOT GROUPING ─────────────────────────────────────────────
master <- master %>%
  mutate(
    EVT_GP_plot = case_when(
      
      # ── CORE CA FORESTS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # CA Mesic Mixed Conifer (fir, pine, Incense Cedar)
      EVT %in% c(2028, 3028) ~ "CA Mesic Mixed Conifer",
      
      # CA Dry-Mesic Mixed Conifer + Jeffrey/ Ponderosa Pine (drought-tolerant species)
      EVT %in% c(2027, 3027, 2031, 3031) ~ "CA Dry Mixed Conifer",
      
      
      # CA Mixed Evergreen (tanoak, live oak with conifers, montac)
      EVT %in% c(2043, 3043, 2014, 3014) ~ "CA Mixed Evergreen Hardwood",
      
      # CA Mixed Oak Woodland
      EVT %in% c(2029, 2030, 3029, 2112, 2113, 2114, 2118, 2008) ~ "CA Mixed Oak Woodland",
      
      # CA Coastal Redwood
      EVT %in% c(2015, 3015) ~ "CA Coastal Redwood",
      
      
      # CA Montane Conifer (lodgepole, subalpine conifers, red fir)
      EVT %in% c(2033, 2044, 2058, 3030, 3033, 2032, 3032) ~ "CA Montane Conifer",
      
      # ── RIPARIAN ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      EVT %in% c(2152, 3138, 3152, 2154) ~ "Riparian",
      
      # ── NON-FOREST ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Shrubs, forbs, grass-dominated
      EVT %in% c(3098, 3129, 3184, 3114, 3299, 3221,
                 3182, 2184, 2138, 2182) ~ "Non-forest",
      
      # ── CHAPARRAL ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # California Montane Woodland and Chaparral, Dry-Mesic Chaparral
      EVT %in% c(2098, 2105) ~ "Chaparral Shrubland",
      
      # ── OTHER FOREST (Rare types < 1%) ──────────────────────────────────
      # Serpentine Systems (stress-tolerant shrubs/forbs and sparse trees)
      EVT %in% c(2021, 2022, 2034, 2099, 2170, 3021, 3022, 3034) ~ "Other Forest",
      
      # Other Mixed Forest/Woodland (Juniper, mahogany woodlands)
      EVT %in% c(2017, 2019, 2062, 2203) ~ "Other Forest",
      
      # Other Conifer Forest (non-CA subtype - Aspen-mixed conifer, closed-cone conifer)
      EVT %in% c(2061, 2177) ~ "Other Forest",
      
      # Catch-all for any unmapped codes
      TRUE ~ "Other Forest"
    )
  )

# ── SET ORDERED FACTOR LEVELS ───────────────────────────────────────────────
master$EVT_GP_plot <- factor(master$EVT_GP_plot, 
                             levels = c(
                               "CA Dry Mixed Conifer",
                               "CA Mesic Mixed Conifer",
                               "CA Montane Conifer",
                               "CA Mixed Evergreen Hardwood",
                               "CA Mixed Oak Woodland",
                               "Non-forest",
                               "Riparian",
                               "Other Forest",
                               "CA Coastal Redwood",
                               "Chaparral Shrubland"
                               
                             ))

# ── VERIFICATION: CHECK DISTRIBUTION OF EVT_GP_PLOT ────────────────────────
cat("\n╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
cat("║  EVT_GP_PLOT DISTRIBUTION (Burned Clean Plots)                 ║\n")
cat("╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")

summary_evt <- master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Burned_clean") %>%
  distinct(plot_key, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  count(EVT_GP_plot, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1),
    cumulative_pct = round(100 * cumsum(n) / sum(n), 1)
  )

print(summary_evt, n = Inf)

cat("\n")
cat("Total n (burned clean plots):", 
    master %>%
      filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Burned_clean") %>%
      distinct(plot_key, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
      nrow(), 
    "\n")

# ── CHECK FOR ANY UNMAPPED EVT CODES ────────────────────────────────────────
cat("\n╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n")
cat("║  UNMAPPED EVT CODES (if any exist)                             ║\n")
cat("╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\n")

unmapped <- master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Burned_clean") %>%
  distinct(plot_key, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(is.na(EVT_GP_plot)) %>%
  nrow()

if (unmapped > 0) {
  cat("WARNING: Found", unmapped, "plots with unmapped EVT codes\n")
  
  master %>%
    filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Burned_clean",
           is.na(EVT_GP_plot)) %>%
    distinct(plot_key, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    count(EVT, evt_name, sort = TRUE) %>%
    print(n = Inf)
} else {
  cat("✓ All EVT codes successfully mapped\n")
}
```

Use the look-up table and replace the old EVT_GP_collapsed and EVT_GP_plot data from data frames using the corrected categories in master:
```{r}
replace_evt_groups <- function(df, lookup) {

  # Remove old grouping variables before joining the authoritative versions
  df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      -any_of(c("EVT_GP_plot"))
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      lookup %>%
        dplyr::select(
          plot_key,
          EVT_GP_plot
        ),
      by = "plot_key"
    )
}

plot_metrics_analysis <- replace_evt_groups(
  plot_metrics_analysis,
  evt_lookup
)

plot_metrics_final <- replace_evt_groups(
  plot_metrics_final,
  evt_lookup
)

dt3 <- replace_evt_groups(
  dt3,
  evt_lookup
)

# Remove EVT_GP_collapsed from dt3, use the EVT_GP_plot data
```
Check the replacements worked:
```{r}
# Check that all three data frames now agree with master

check_evt_groups <- function(df, df_name) {

  df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      plot_key,
      EVT_GP_plot
    ) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    left_join(
      evt_lookup %>%
        dplyr::select(
          plot_key,
          master_EVT_GP_plot = EVT_GP_plot
        ),
      by = "plot_key"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      plot_match =
        as.character(EVT_GP_plot) ==
        as.character(master_EVT_GP_plot)
    ) %>%
    summarise(
      data_frame = df_name,
      n = n(),
      plot_mismatches = sum(!plot_match, na.rm = TRUE),
      missing_master_plot = sum(is.na(master_EVT_GP_plot))
    )
}

bind_rows(
  check_evt_groups(
    plot_metrics_analysis,
    "plot_metrics_analysis"
  ),
  check_evt_groups(
    plot_metrics_final,
    "plot_metrics_final"
  ),
  check_evt_groups(
    dt3,
    "dt3"
  )
)

table(plot_metrics_analysis$EVT_GP_plot)
```

Total CA area by EVT type as reported in Table 3.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# ============================================================
# 1. PLOT DATA
# ============================================================

plot_area_ha <- pi * 56^2 / 10000  # 0.9852 ha per plot

evt_table <- tribble(
  ~EVT_GP_plot,                    ~n_plots,
  "CA Dry Mixed Conifer",          2532,
  "CA Mesic Mixed Conifer",        2355,
  "CA Montane Conifer",            1306,
  "CA Mixed Evergreen Hardwood",   1108,
  "CA Mixed Oak Woodland",          971,
  "Non-Forest",                     938,
  "Riparian",                       759,
  "Other Forest",                   583,
  "CA Coastal Redwood",             483,
  "Chaparral Shrubland",            305
) %>%
  mutate(
    area_in_plots_ha = n_plots * plot_area_ha,
    pct_of_plot_area = 100 * n_plots / sum(n_plots)
  )


# ============================================================
# 2. READ STATEWIDE EVT DATA FROM GEE CSV
# ============================================================

# Change this path to wherever you saved the GEE CSV
statewide_data <- read_csv(
  "CA_EVT_Statewide_Coverage.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# 3. CALIFORNIA TOTAL AREA
# ============================================================

# From the GEE calculation:
total_ca_ha <- 42396761.49709419


# ============================================================
# 4. CLEAN STATEWIDE DATA
# ============================================================

statewide_data <- statewide_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Make sure area is numeric
    Area_ha = as.numeric(Area_ha),

    # Recalculate rather than relying on the CSV value
    # so the denominator is explicitly ALL of California
    pct_of_ca = 100 * Area_ha / total_ca_ha
  ) %>%
  select(
    EVT_Group,
    Area_ha,
    Area_km2,
    EVT_Codes,
    pct_of_ca
  )


# Check statewide data
print(statewide_data)


# ============================================================
# 5. COMBINE PLOT + STATEWIDE DATA
# ============================================================

final_table <- evt_table %>%
  left_join(
    statewide_data,
    by = c("EVT_GP_plot" = "EVT_Group")
  ) %>%
  select(
    EVT_GP_plot,
    n_plots,
    area_in_plots_ha,
    pct_of_plot_area,
    Area_ha,
    Area_km2,
    pct_of_ca,
    EVT_Codes
  ) %>%
  rename(
    "EVT Group" = EVT_GP_plot,
    "N Plots" = n_plots,
    "Area in Plots (ha)" = area_in_plots_ha,
    "% of Plot Area" = pct_of_plot_area,
    "CA Area (ha)" = Area_ha,
    "CA Area (km2)" = Area_km2,
    "% of CA" = pct_of_ca,
    "EVT Codes" = EVT_Codes
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Area in Plots (ha)` = round(`Area in Plots (ha)`, 2),
    `% of Plot Area` = round(`% of Plot Area`, 1),
    `CA Area (ha)` = round(`CA Area (ha)`, 2),
    `CA Area (km2)` = round(`CA Area (km2)`, 2),
    `% of CA` = round(`% of CA`, 2)
  )


# ============================================================
# 6. VIEW FINAL TABLE
# ============================================================

print(final_table)


# ============================================================
# 7. SANITY CHECKS
# ============================================================

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("SANITY CHECKS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

cat(
  "Total California area:",
  format(total_ca_ha, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
  "ha\n"
)

cat(
  "Selected EVT area:",
  format(sum(statewide_data$Area_ha), big.mark = ",",
         scientific = FALSE),
  "ha\n"
)

cat(
  "Selected EVT area as % of CA:",
  round(
    100 * sum(statewide_data$Area_ha) / total_ca_ha,
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)

cat(
  "Remaining / other CA area:",
  format(
    total_ca_ha - sum(statewide_data$Area_ha),
    big.mark = ",",
    scientific = FALSE
  ),
  "ha\n"
)

cat(
  "Remaining / other CA:",
  round(
    100 * (total_ca_ha - sum(statewide_data$Area_ha)) /
      total_ca_ha,
    2
  ),
  "%\n"
)
```

How min_canopy is created in master
```{r}
min_post1_dt <- master[
  delta_year >= 1 &
  delta_year <= 10,

  .(
    min_canopy = min(TRE, na.rm = TRUE),

    # year where TRE reached minimum
    min_year = delta_year[which.min(TRE)]
  ),

  by = plot_key
]

min_post1_dt <- master[
  delta_year >= 1 &
  delta_year <= 10,

  .(
    min_canopy = min(TRE, na.rm = TRUE),

    # year where TRE reached minimum
    min_year = delta_year[which.min(TRE)]
  ),

  by = plot_key
]

# ── Step 2: Create event indicator ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Recreate event_observed explicitly
min_post1_dt[
  ,
  event_observed := ifelse(min_year < 10, 1, 0)
]

# Check it exists
names(min_post1_dt)

table(min_post1_dt$event_observed, useNA = "ifany")
names(master)


master <- master%>%
  left_join(
    as.data.frame(
      min_post1_dt[, .(
        plot_key,
        min_canopy,
        min_year,
        event_observed
      )]
    ),
    by = "plot_key"
  )

# ── Step 4: Verify ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
summary(master$min_year)

table(master$min_year, useNA = "ifany")
summary(master$min_canopy, useNA = "ifany")

sum(master$min_year == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
    ),
    
    yr10_TRE = mean(
      TRE[delta_year == 10],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    min_canopy = mean(min_canopy, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rel_change_gain = yr10_TRE - min_canopy,
    rel_change_loss = (min_canopy - baseline_final) / baseline_final * 100
  )

sev_yr10_unburned
```

The ~1,049 censored plots (event_observed == 0) are likely:

Heavily weighted toward low-moderate severity (still have canopy to lose)
Higher elevation (slower decline rates)
Lower dNBR (gradual mortality patterns)

These censored plots are driving the negative quantile regression at the 90th percentile because they represent scenarios where delayed mortality can still accumulate despite low immediate loss.

The weak plot-level correlation between immediate and delayed canopy loss (r = 0.008, Figure 5) masks an important subpopulation of high-severity burned plots that continue experiencing delayed mortality through post-fire year 10. Approximately 9.4% of burned plots (n = 1,067) had not reached minimum canopy cover by year 10, with 42.3% of these censored plots occurring in high-severity burns (mean dNBR = 574). Importantly, these high-severity censored plots maintained high proportions of delayed mortality (mean = 58.4%), despite already sustaining substantial immediate losses. This pattern suggests that high-severity fires create persistent environmental conditions—including ongoing physiological stress, root pathogen infection, competition release, and drought exposure—that sustain elevated mortality rates in surviving trees even years after the initial fire event. The censored plots thus represent not canopy-availability limitation, but rather environmental stress persistence: sites where post-fire conditions continue driving tree death beyond the typical year 1-5 trajectory. This explains the apparent contradiction between population-level trajectories showing high-severity fires with large absolute delayed losses (Figure 2) and plot-level analyses showing weak immediate-delayed correlation (Figure 5)—the correlation is weakened by this subpopulation of high-severity sites that maintain delayed-dominant mortality pathways despite limited residual canopy.

```{r}
  distinct(plot_key, Correct_Plot_Label_final, Severity_mean) %>%
  group_by(Correct_Plot_Label_final) %>%
  summarise(
    n_plots       = n(),
    n_na_sev      = sum(is.na(Severity_mean)),
    n_with_sev    = sum(!is.na(Severity_mean)),
    pct_na        = round(100 * n_na_sev / n(), 1)
  )
# Expected:
# Burned_clean:   0 NAs
# Unburned_clean: ~100% NAs

# If any Unburned_clean have severity — flag them
unburned_with_sev <- master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Unburned_clean",
         !is.na(Severity_mean)) %>%
  distinct(plot_key, Severity_mean, elevation, aspect)

cat('Unburned plots with severity values:', nrow(unburned_with_sev), '\n')

# ── STRATIFICATION TABLES WITH ACTUAL % ───────────────────────────────────────
# Burned strata
burned_strat_full <- master %>%
  distinct(plot_key, burned_stratum, sev_class, elev_class) %>%
  filter(!is.na(burned_stratum)) %>%
  count(sev_class, elev_class, burned_stratum) %>%
  mutate(
    total_burned  = sum(n),
    pct_of_burned = round(100 * n / total_burned, 1),
    expected_n    = 175 * 20, #number of fires * 20 plots/ strata
    pct_expected  = round(100 * n / expected_n, 1)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(sev_class, elev_class, n, pct_of_burned, expected_n, pct_expected) %>%
  arrange(sev_class, elev_class)

print(burned_strat_full)

# UNBURNED STRATA
# 3 elevation classes × 2 aspect classes = 6 strata (will report all burned and unburned clean data)

strat_by_plot_label <- master %>%
  filter(
    Correct_Plot_Label_final %in% c("Burned_clean", "Unburned_clean"),
    !is.na(elev_class),
    !is.na(asp_class)
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    plot_key,
    Correct_Plot_Label_final,
    elev_class,
    asp_class
  ) %>%
  count(
    Correct_Plot_Label_final,
    elev_class,
    asp_class,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Correct_Plot_Label_final) %>%
  mutate(
    total_plots = sum(n),
    pct_within_plot_label = round(100 * n / total_plots, 1),
    expected_n = 175 * 30,
    pct_expected = round(100 * n / expected_n, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Correct_Plot_Label_final,
    elev_class,
    asp_class,
    n,
    total_plots,
    pct_within_plot_label,
    expected_n,
    pct_expected
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    Correct_Plot_Label_final,
    elev_class,
    asp_class
  )

print(strat_by_plot_label, n = Inf)

# ── ECOLOGICAL NOTE ON BURNED STRATA IMBALANCE ────────────────────────────────
# Low severity strata are underrepresented (2-5% of expected)
# This is ecologically expected — large CA wildfires selected for size
# tend to burn at moderate-high severity
# High x Moderate (95.7%) and High x Low (78.2%) are well sampled
# Flag low severity strata in methods as a study limitation

# How many fires have ANY low severity plots?
master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Burned_clean",
         sev_class == "Low") %>%
  summarise(n_fires = n_distinct(Fire_ID),
            n_plots = n_distinct(plot_key))
```

## Figures

#Study Domain Map: Figure 1
The map of CA with sample burn perimeters and all 1984-2024 fire perimeters was created in ArcGIS Pro from shape files provided within the provided shared GitHub script below: (https://github.com/bhays4days/delayed-mortality-california.git)

#Figure 2. Mean burned plot canopy loss stratified by dNBR burn severity:
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

sev_levels <- c("Low", "Moderate", "High")

master <- master %>%
  mutate(sev_MT07 = na_if(trimws(as.character(sev_MT07)), ""),
         sev_MT07 = if_else(sev_MT07 %in% sev_levels, sev_MT07, NA_character_))

table(master$sev_MT07, useNA = "always")

master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Burned_clean") %>%
  distinct(plot_key, sev_MT07) %>%
  count(sev_MT07)

evts_ordered <- c(
"CA Dry Mixed Conifer",
 "CA Mesic Mixed Conifer",
  "CA Montane Conifer",
   "CA Mixed Evergreen Hardwood",
     "CA Mixed Oak Woodland",
       "Non-forest",
         "Riparian",
           "Other Forest",
             "CA Coastal Redwood",
               "Chaparral Shrubland"
)


master <- master %>%
  mutate(
    TRE            = as.numeric(TRE),
    baseline_final = as.numeric(baseline_final)
  )

# confirm no silent NAs were introduced by the coercion
sum(is.na(master$TRE))          # compare with the pre-coercion NA count
sum(is.na(master$baseline_final))

burned_dev <- master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Burned_clean",
         EVT_GP_plot %in% evts_ordered,
         delta_year >= 0, delta_year <= 10,
         !is.na(baseline_final)) %>%
  mutate(canopy_dev = TRE - baseline_final)

dev_summary <- burned_dev %>%
  group_by(EVT_GP_plot, sev_MT07, delta_year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean_dev = mean(canopy_dev, na.rm = TRUE),
            se_dev   = sd(canopy_dev, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 10)

```

```{r}

sev_colors <- c("High" = "#B2182B", "Moderate" = "#E08214", "Low" = "#4DAC26")

# ── Panel A: burned canopy trajectories by severity ──────────────────────────
panelA_data <- master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Burned_clean",
         delta_year >= -10, delta_year <= 10,
         !is.na(sev_MT07)) %>% # now this should work
  mutate(sev_MT07 = factor(sev_MT07, levels = c("High", "Moderate", "Low"))) %>%
  group_by(delta_year, sev_MT07) %>%
  summarise(n      = n(),
            mean_cc = mean(TRE, na.rm = TRUE),
            se_cc   = sd(TRE, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
            ci95_low  = mean_cc - 1.96 * se_cc,
            ci95_high = mean_cc + 1.96 * se_cc,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 10)

nrow(panelA_data)                 # expect ~60-63 rows (21 years × 3 severities)
count(panelA_data, sev_MT07)      # 3 levels only, ~21 rows each

panelA_minimum <- panelA_data %>%
  filter(delta_year >= 1) %>%
  group_by(sev_MT07) %>%
  slice_min(mean_cc, n = 1) %>% ungroup()

unburned_data <- master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Unburned_clean",
         delta_year >= -10, delta_year <= 10) %>%
  group_by(delta_year) %>%
  summarise(n      = n(),
            mean_cc = mean(TRE, na.rm = TRUE),
            se_cc   = sd(TRE, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
            ci95_low  = mean_cc - 1.96 * se_cc,
            ci95_high = mean_cc + 1.96 * se_cc,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 10)

# ── Panel B deviations, using the manuscript baseline (years -5..-1) ─────────
# Burned: baseline_final already exists per plot from the validated pipeline

# Unburned: same -5..-1 window, for methodological symmetry
unburned_baseline <- master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Unburned_clean",
         delta_year >= -5, delta_year <= -1) %>%
  group_by(plot_key) %>%
  summarise(baseline_unb = mean(TRE, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

unburned_summary <- master %>%
  filter(Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Unburned_clean",
         EVT_GP_plot %in% evts_ordered,
         delta_year >= 0, delta_year <= 10) %>%
  left_join(unburned_baseline, by = "plot_key") %>%
  mutate(canopy_dev = TRE - baseline_unb) %>%
  filter(!is.na(baseline_unb)) %>%
  group_by(EVT_GP_plot, delta_year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean_dev_unb = mean(canopy_dev, na.rm = TRUE),
            se_dev_unb   = sd(canopy_dev, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 10)
```

#Figure 2 run on ALL EVT_GP_plot groups n= 10 RElative Canopy loss

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(ggnewscale)
library(cowplot)

sev_levels <- c("Low", "Moderate", "High")

sev_colors <- c(
  "High"     = "#B2182B",
  "Moderate" = "#E08214",
  "Low"      = "#4DAC26"
)

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PANEL A: Severity Trajectories
#   fixes: theme chain repaired, x-axis title restored, y-axis starts at 15
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
fig2a <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +

  # ── Unburned control (dashed grey) ──────────────────────────────────────
  geom_ribbon(data = unburned_data,
              aes(x = delta_year, ymin = ci95_low, ymax = ci95_high),
              alpha = 0.15, fill = "grey50") +
  geom_line(data = unburned_data,
            aes(x = delta_year, y = mean_cc),
            linetype = "twodash", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.8) +

  # ── Burned, by severity ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  geom_ribbon(data = panelA_data,
              aes(x = delta_year, ymin = ci95_low, ymax = ci95_high,
                  fill = sev_MT07, group = sev_MT07),
              alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  geom_line(data = panelA_data,
            aes(x = delta_year, y = mean_cc, color = sev_MT07, group = sev_MT07),
            linewidth = 0.9) +

  # ── Stars at post-fire minimum ──────────────────────────────────────────
  geom_point(data = panelA_minimum,
             aes(x = delta_year, y = mean_cc, color = sev_MT07),
             shape = 8, size = 3.5, stroke = 1.2, show.legend = FALSE) +

  # ── Immediate / delayed annotations ─────────────────────────────────────
  annotate("segment", x = 0.1, xend = 1.0, y = 65, yend = 42,
           arrow = arrow(ends = "last", length = unit(0.15, "cm")), color = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = 2.3, y = 48, label = "Immediate\nCanopy Loss",
           size = 4.2, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 0.9) +
  annotate("segment", x = 1.2, xend = 2.2, y = 42, yend = 23,
           arrow = arrow(ends = "last", length = unit(0.15, "cm")), color = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = 3.8, y = 30, label = "Delayed Canopy Loss",
           size = 4.2, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 0.9) +

  scale_color_manual(values = sev_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-10, 10, by = 2),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.02))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(15, 70, by = 5),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(15, 70)) +
  labs(x = "Years since fire ignition",
       y = "Mean tree canopy cover (%)",
       title = "A. Canopy Loss by Burn Severity") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12, base_family = "Arial") +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12, margin = margin(t = 2)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text    = element_text(size = 11, color = "black"),
    axis.line    = element_line(linewidth = 0.45, color = "black"),
    axis.ticks   = element_line(linewidth = 0.45, color = "black"),
    plot.title   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.margin  = margin(4, 4, 4, 4, "pt")
  )

fig2a

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PANEL B: Forest Type Trajectories, faceted, 4 columns
#   fixes: full geom layers restored, white panels, legend in blank last-row slot
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
evts_ordered <- c(
  "CA Dry Mixed Conifer",
  "CA Mesic Mixed Conifer",
  "CA Montane Conifer",
  "CA Mixed Evergreen Hardwood",
  "CA Mixed Oak Woodland",
  "Non-forest",
  "Riparian",
  "Other Forest",
  "CA Coastal Redwood",
  "Chaparral Shrubland"
)

tre_evt_all <- master %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    EVT_GP_plot %in% evts_ordered,
    delta_year >= -10,
    delta_year <= 10,
    !is.na(EVT_GP_plot)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    burn_status = case_when(
      Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Burned_clean"   ~ "Burned",
      Correct_Plot_Label_final == "Unburned_clean" ~ "Unburned",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(burn_status))

# Normalize burned plots to year-1 post-fire baseline
norm_baseline_evt <- tre_evt_all %>%
  filter(burn_status == "Burned", delta_year == 1) %>%
  dplyr::select(plot_key, TRE_yr1 = TRE)

tre_evt_all <- tre_evt_all %>%
  left_join(norm_baseline_evt, by = "plot_key") %>%
  mutate(
    TRE_norm = case_when(
      burn_status == "Burned" & !is.na(TRE_yr1) ~ TRE - TRE_yr1,
      burn_status == "Unburned" ~
        TRE - mean(TRE[burn_status == "Unburned" & delta_year == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(TRE_norm))

# Aggregate by forest type, severity, and year
tre_evt_summary <- tre_evt_all %>%
  group_by(EVT_GP_plot, delta_year, sev_MT07, burn_status) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    mean_TRE = mean(TRE, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_TRE   = sd(TRE, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
    ci_upper = mean_TRE + 1.96 * se_TRE,
    ci_lower = mean_TRE - 1.96 * se_TRE,
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n >= 10)

# ── Minimum points for BURNED plots only (per EVT x severity) ───────────────
evt_sev_minimum <- tre_evt_summary %>%
  filter(burn_status == "Burned", delta_year >= 1) %>%
  group_by(EVT_GP_plot, sev_MT07) %>%
  slice_min(mean_TRE, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# ── Factor ordering ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
tre_evt_summary <- tre_evt_summary %>%
  mutate(
    EVT_GP_plot = factor(EVT_GP_plot, levels = evts_ordered),
    sev_MT07    = factor(sev_MT07, levels = c("High", "Moderate", "Low")),
    burn_status = factor(burn_status, levels = c("Unburned", "Burned"))
  )

evt_sev_minimum <- evt_sev_minimum %>%
  mutate(
    EVT_GP_plot = factor(EVT_GP_plot, levels = evts_ordered),
    sev_MT07    = factor(sev_MT07, levels = c("High", "Moderate", "Low"))
  )

# ── Faceted panel B ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig2b <- ggplot(tre_evt_summary,
                aes(x = delta_year, y = mean_TRE,
                    color = sev_MT07, fill = sev_MT07,
                    linetype = burn_status)) +

  # Confidence interval ribbons for burned only
  geom_ribbon(data = filter(tre_evt_summary, burn_status == "Burned"),
              aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper),
              alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +

  # Mean lines
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +

  # Stars at minimum points for burned plots only
  geom_point(data = evt_sev_minimum,
             aes(x = delta_year, y = mean_TRE, color = sev_MT07),
             shape = 8, size = 2, stroke = 1.2, show.legend = FALSE) +

  # Reference lines
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "twodash", color = "grey30",
             linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40",
             linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +

  # Facet by forest type: 4 per row (4 + 4 + 2)
  facet_wrap(~EVT_GP_plot, ncol = 4, scales = "fixed") +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = sev_colors,
    name   = "Burn Severity",
    breaks = c("High", "Moderate", "Low")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("Burned" = "solid", "Unburned" = "twodash"),
    name   = "Plot Type",
    labels = c("Burned" = "Burned", "Unburned" = "Unburned Control")
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-10, 10, by = 2)) +

  labs(
    title = "B. Canopy Loss by Burn Severity and Forest Type",
    x     = "Years Since Fire Ignition",
    y     = "Mean tree canopy cover (%)"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    strip.text       = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text        = element_text(size = 11, color = "black"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "grey75",
                                    linewidth = 0.3),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing    = unit(8, "pt"),
    legend.position      = c(0.52, 0.06),
    legend.justification = c(0, 0),
    legend.box           = "horizontal",       # CHANGED: guides left/right of each other
    legend.background    = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "grey70",

    legend.text          = element_text(size = 11)

  )

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# COMBINE PANELS A & B (white everywhere, fig2b keeps its internal legend)
```
